turns.question: Where is the structural map engine implemented, and how is the parser engine selected per file?
turns.text:
The README already points to `internal/mapengine/`. Let me look at its structure and the routing logic directly.Now let me read the actual routing logic — `mapAuto` and `Map` in types.go, plus `normalizeEngine` to see the selection rules.I have everything needed to answer confidently.

## Structural map engine

**Location:** `internal/mapengine/` — a self-contained Go package implementing the `--map` feature (per README: "parser-backed structural map (~92% token reduction)").

Files (confirmed via `ghx tree`):
- `types.go` — shared types (`Engine`, `Level`, `Kind`, `Mapper` interface, `Result`, `Symbol`) and the top-level dispatch (`Map`, `mapAuto`, `mapTreeSitterWithFallback`, `buildResultFromSymbols`)
- `goast.go` — `GoASTMapper`, built on Go's own `go/ast`
- `treesitter.go` — `TreeSitterMapper`, built on `gotreesitter` (`odvcencio/gotreesitter`), with per-language tag-query configs (`defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs`, `TreeSitterLanguageConfig`)
- `regex.go` / `regex_test.go` — `RegexMapper`, the generic fallback

The common contract is the `Mapper` interface (`internal/mapengine/types.go:47`): `Map(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error)`. All three mappers (`GoASTMapper`, `TreeSitterMapper`, `RegexMapper`) implement it.

## Engine selection per file

Selection happens in `internal/mapengine/types.go`, function `Map` (line 125) → `mapAuto` (line 143):

```go
func Map(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error) {
    opts = NormalizeOptions(opts)
    switch opts.Engine {
    case EngineRegex:      return RegexMapper{}.Map(...)
    case EngineTreeSitter: return mapTreeSitterWithFallback(...)
    case EngineAuto:       return mapAuto(...)
    default:               // unknown value → regex fallback + warning
    }
}

func mapAuto(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error) {
    switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
    case ".go":
        // GoASTMapper, falls back to regex on parse error
    case ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".py", ".rs":
        // TreeSitterMapper, falls back to regex on failure
    default:
        // RegexMapper directly
    }
}
```

So selection is **by file extension** in `auto` mode (the default):
- `.go` → `GoASTMapper` (falls back to `RegexMapper` on any AST parse error)
- `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.jsx`/`.py`/`.rs` → `TreeSitterMapper` via `mapTreeSitterWithFallback` (falls back to `RegexMapper` if tree-sitter errors, e.g. `ErrUnsupportedLanguage`)
- everything else → `RegexMapper` directly

This matches the README's claim exactly ("Go uses go/ast; TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Rust use tree-sitter... everything else falls back to regex").

**Override path (CLI wiring):**
- `internal/cli/ghx.go:112,211` — the `read` command exposes a `--map-engine` flag (default `"auto"`, choices `auto|regex|tree-sitter`), read via `cmd.Flags().GetString("map-engine")`.
- `internal/ghx/read.go:39,187-190` — `ReadOpts.MapEngine` is passed straight through into `mapengine.Options{Engine: mapengine.Engine(opts.MapEngine), ...}` and handed to `mapengine.Map`.
- `internal/mapengine/types.go:80` — `normalizeEngine` lowercases/trims the value and maps anything not literally `"regex"` or `"tree-sitter"` to `EngineAuto`, so an invalid/empty flag silently becomes auto-detection.

Within `TreeSitterMapper.Map` (`treesitter.go:25`), the specific tree-sitter grammar is further resolved per file via `treeSitterEntry(path)` (line 89), which looks up the language grammar from the `gotreesitter/grammars` package by extension, and `treeSitterConfigForEntry` (line 101) fetches the matching `TreeSitterLanguageConfig` (tag queries, kind mapping, signature formatting) for that language.

**Not verified:** I did not read the full bodies of `regex.go`, `goast.go`'s symbol-extraction internals, or `treesitter.go`'s tag-query definitions beyond their signatures (only structural maps were pulled, not full file content) — so exact per-language query strings and the regex engine's pattern set are unconfirmed beyond function names.

README:
# ghx — the code-reconnaissance sidecar for AI agents

**Expensive main agents shouldn't burn frontier tokens on tree/grep/read loops.**
ghx is a cheap, specialized **sidecar agent** that a main agent delegates code
reconnaissance to. Ask it a repo question in plain English; it explores GitHub
under the hood and hands back a **schema-validated evidence report** — claims
with citations, the commands it ran, and what it could not confirm — while every
artifact of the investigation lands on disk under `~/.ghx/sessions/` for you or
the parent agent to inspect.

This is the first public cut of the **Agent Sidecar Framework**: a main agent
delegates a whole competence domain to a proficient specialist instead of loading
that domain's tools and doctrine into its own context. ghx is the proof — the
code-reconnaissance sidecar — and, underneath it, a sharp standalone GitHub
exploration CLI. The durable vision lives in
[docs/NORTH_STAR.md](docs/NORTH_STAR.md).

> ghx is two products in one binary: a **sidecar brain** you delegate to (this
> README's lead), and the **classic exploration CLI** it drives under the hood
> (documented in full further down). Use whichever fits; they share one core.

## Why a sidecar

When a main agent stops mid-task to explore code, the real cost is not the API
calls — it is the context. Exploration output floods the window, the agent loses
the thread of the engineering work, and the ~400 lines of tool doctrine it needs
to explore well are dead weight it re-pays every sessi
